adapters.name: Plain HTML and CSS
adapters.description: This is the reference adapter for rendering GOV.UK interfaces without a component framework. Later framework adapters must preserve the same DOM, asset, server-rendering and enhancement contracts.
adapters.fixtureDescription: The development fixture at `fixtures/vertical-slice/index.html` exercises Button, Text input and Accordion against the exact reviewed dependency. It is test evidence, not package payload or a starter application.
requirements: Render complete semantic HTML on the server or in the initial document; JavaScript must enhance usable content rather than create the only usable version.
Copy markup and class contracts from the focused component records under design/govuk/components instead of recreating components from their appearance.
Use the pinned govuk-frontend component CSS and JavaScript for production components. The portable CSS variables are for project extensions and interoperability, not a replacement for component CSS.
Keep native form controls, labels, hints, errors, fieldsets, legends, heading hierarchy and ID relationships intact.
Confirm that the service is eligible before deploying GDS Transport, the GOV.UK crown or other protected identity assets; this package does not redistribute them.
assetSetup: Install the reviewed implementation with npm install govuk-frontend@6.5.0 --save-exact.
Copy dist/govuk/govuk-frontend.min.css and dist/govuk/govuk-frontend.min.js to a public URL controlled by the service. Copy source maps when production diagnostics require them.
Copy dist/govuk/assets to the public /assets path expected by the compiled CSS, or compile Sass with an explicitly reviewed asset-path configuration.

Load GOV.UK Frontend CSS before service-specific CSS. Put reviewed service overrides in a separate stylesheet and use tokens/govuk.css only for custom UI that is not already supplied by GOV.UK Frontend.
Do not hotlink assets from the Design System website and do not copy this repository's extraction screenshots or fonts into the service.
rendering: Return the page shell, skip link, main landmark, form controls, validation messages and component content in the initial HTML response.
Use one unique ID for each labelled or described element and keep for, aria-describedby, aria-labelledby and href fragment references resolvable.
On validation failure, render the Error summary and inline errors on the server, retain safe user input and move focus only through the official enhancement behaviour.
Keep links as links and buttons as buttons. Use a link styled as a button only for navigation, and preserve its href.
Do not hide Accordion or Tabs content in the unenhanced document; GOV.UK Frontend applies enhanced disclosure behaviour after initialisation.
progressiveEnhancement: Place the official body-class detection snippet immediately after the opening body element so supported browsers receive js-enabled and govuk-frontend-supported before components initialise.
Add the documented data-module attribute only to components that GOV.UK Frontend enhances.
Load the JavaScript entry point as a module near the end of body and call initAll once for the initial document.
Every form journey and essential action must remain usable when JavaScript fails, is blocked or is unsupported.
When a Content Security Policy blocks inline scripts, apply the service's nonce or hash policy to the early body-class snippet without delaying it until after page rendering.
lifecycle: Initial document: call initAll() after the component markup exists in the DOM.
Inserted fragment: insert complete component markup into a container, then call initAll(container) so only new descendants are discovered.
Do not repeatedly call initAll() over the whole document; GOV.UK Frontend marks initialised roots and duplicate initialisation is an error.
If application code removes enhanced markup, discard references to that DOM. Re-render a complete unenhanced component before initialising its replacement.
Treat console initialisation errors as test failures and verify keyboard, focus and no-JavaScript behaviour for every interactive component used.
adapters.pageTemplateIntro: Render the page shell on the server. Replace the comment with complete markup from the relevant focused component records.
adapters.pageTemplate: Skip to main content

adapters.name: React
adapters.description: This adapter renders official GOV.UK markup through React while leaving GOV.UK Frontend responsible for its own progressive enhancement. Its boundary model is intentionally conservative because GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 mutates enhanced DOM and does not expose a general teardown API.
adapters.fixtureDescription: The development SSR and hydration fixture starts with `npm run fixture:serve:react` and renders `fixtures/react/app.mjs`. It exercises Button, Text input and Accordion with React 19.3.0 and GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0. The fixture is test evidence, not package payload or a starter application.
requirements: Render complete GOV.UK page and component markup on the server or at build time, then hydrate it. Do not make client-only React rendering the only path to content, form controls or essential actions.
Translate official HTML to JSX mechanically: use className for class and htmlFor for label for, while preserving elements, GOV.UK classes, IDs, data-module attributes and ARIA relationships.
Treat a GOV.UK Frontend-enhanced subtree as externally managed after initialisation. Do not use React state or prop changes to reconcile descendants that GOV.UK Frontend has mutated.

Render only passive component markup inside an enhancement boundary. Keep React stateful controls outside it because descendant state updates can still reconcile DOM even when the boundary's incoming children are frozen.
Use the pinned govuk-frontend component CSS and JavaScript. Portable tokens remain for service-owned extensions and interoperability, not for recreating GOV.UK components.
Keep native form controls and server-render validation. Confirm separately that the service may use GDS Transport, the GOV.UK crown and other protected identity assets.
assetSetup: Install the reviewed implementation with npm install govuk-frontend@6.5.0 --save-exact and use the React and React DOM versions supported by the host application. The fixture pins react@19.3.0 and react-dom@19.3.0 only to make its evidence reproducible.
Import GOV.UK Frontend Sass or CSS through the host build, or copy dist/govuk/govuk-frontend.min.css to a public path. Copy dist/govuk/assets to the URL expected by the compiled CSS.
Import govuk-frontend from client-only code or through a dynamic import. The package references browser globals when evaluated, so do not eagerly evaluate its JavaScript in the server runtime.
Load GOV.UK Frontend styles before service styles. Do not replace component CSS with tokens, CSS-in-JS or a React component library.
Do not hotlink Design System assets and do not distribute extraction screenshots or fonts from this repository.
rendering: Use the host framework's server renderer or static renderer for production. The small fixture uses renderToString only because it has no asynchronous data; React recommends streaming server APIs where they fit the runtime.

Hydrate server-rendered output with hydrateRoot and pass the same initial React tree and data. Treat hydration mismatch warnings as defects rather than suppressing them, except for the body class intentionally changed by the early GOV.UK support snippet.
Keep deterministic IDs between server and client. When useId is used across multiple roots, keep identifierPrefix identical in the server and hydrateRoot options.
Render Error summary, inline errors and safe submitted values on the server after validation. Preserve for, aria-describedby and focus-target relationships exactly.
Keep Accordion and Tabs content in the server HTML. GOV.UK Frontend applies disclosure state only after React hydration has committed.
progressiveEnhancement: Place the official body-class detection snippet immediately after the opening body element in the server-rendered page shell; do not wait for a React Effect to add support classes.
Hydrate the existing server markup. Do not call createRoot for content that was server-rendered, because that discards the progressive-enhancement baseline.
After hydration commits, initialise GOV.UK Frontend once within a stable boundary. Use a ref for the scope and surface initialisation errors to the application's error reporting.
Guard one-time initialisation because React Strict Mode runs an extra development Effect cycle. Never solve the duplicate by disabling useful React checks globally.
Every journey must remain usable without the client bundle. Apply the service Content Security Policy nonce or hash to the early inline body-class script.
lifecycle: Initial render: hydrate first, then initialise each stable boundary once. The example WeakSet prevents a second initialisation of the same DOM scope during React Strict Mode checks.
Freeze the boundary's initial children so parent renders cannot make React reconcile DOM that GOV.UK Frontend has enhanced.
For genuinely new content, mount a fresh boundary with complete unenhanced markup and a new key. Never call initAll over an existing enhanced root.

To replace enhanced content, unmount the whole boundary instead of changing descendants in place. Prefer full-page navigation for frequently changing interactive regions because GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 has no general public destroy lifecycle.
Test server HTML with JavaScript disabled, hydration without mismatches, keyboard and focus behaviour, repeated Strict Mode Effects, whole-boundary replacement and a clean browser console.
adapters.pageTemplateIntro: Render this page component and service tree on the server, emit the doctype, and hydrate the identical tree on the client. The early body script is static trusted source text, never user content.

adapters.name: Angular
adapters.description: This adapter server-renders official GOV.UK markup with Angular, hydrates that markup unchanged, and delays GOV.UK Frontend DOM enhancement until Angular has completed its initial client render. Enhanced component subtrees stay static because GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 mutates their DOM and exposes no general teardown API.
adapters.fixtureDescription: The development SSR and hydration fixture starts with `npm run fixture:serve:angular` and renders `fixtures/angular/app.mjs`. It exercises Button, Text input and Accordion with Angular 22.1.6 and GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0. The fixture is test evidence, not package payload or a starter application, and requires a Node version supported by Angular 22.
requirements: Render complete GOV.UK page and component markup with Angular SSR or prerendering. Do not make client-side rendering the only path to content, form controls or essential actions.

Translate official HTML into Angular templates mechanically. Preserve elements, GOV.UK classes, IDs, for attributes, data-module attributes and ARIA relationships; Angular templates use the normal HTML class and for names.

Keep a GOV.UK Frontend-enhanced subtree static after initialisation. Do not put signals, interpolations, control flow, bound properties or Angular event handlers inside markup that GOV.UK Frontend will mutate.
Use a passive leaf component with OnPush change detection as the enhancement boundary. Keep stateful Angular controls outside it and replace the entire boundary when new content is required.
Use the pinned govuk-frontend component CSS and JavaScript. Portable tokens remain for service-owned extensions and interoperability, not for recreating GOV.UK components.
Keep native form controls and server-rendered validation. Confirm separately that the service may use GDS Transport, the GOV.UK crown and other protected identity assets.
assetSetup: Install the reviewed implementation with npm install govuk-frontend@6.5.0 --save-exact and use the Angular versions supported by the host application. The fixture pins Angular 22.1.6 only to make its evidence reproducible.
Enable Angular SSR or prerendering through the Angular CLI and keep provideClientHydration() in the shared application providers used by both server and client bootstraps.
Add GOV.UK Frontend Sass or CSS to the Angular build, or copy dist/govuk/govuk-frontend.min.css to a public path. Copy dist/govuk/assets to the URL expected by the compiled CSS.
Import govuk-frontend only from browser code, normally with a dynamic import after Angular hydration. The package references browser globals and must not be eagerly evaluated by the server runtime.
Load GOV.UK Frontend styles before service styles. Do not replace component CSS with tokens, Angular Material or another component library, and do not hotlink Design System assets.
rendering: Use the Angular SSR or prerender pipeline for production. The compact fixture calls renderApplication directly only to make its server output independently testable; custom server bootstraps must include provideServerRendering() so hydration transfer state is serialized.
Use provideClientHydration() in the common application configuration and render the same component tree and data on the server and client. Treat NG0500, NG0505 and NG0507 diagnostics as defects.

Do not let GOV.UK Frontend or any other third-party script change the Angular application DOM before hydration. Preserve Angular-generated whitespace and comment markers through CDN and HTML processing.
Keep deterministic IDs and valid HTML between server and client. Use the same preserveWhitespaces setting for both builds and explicitly include browser-inserted structures such as tbody.
Render Error summary, inline errors, safe submitted values, Accordion content and Tabs content on the server. GOV.UK Frontend applies disclosure state only after hydration.
progressiveEnhancement: Place the official body-class detection snippet immediately after the opening body element in src/index.html. Keep the Angular application root after that script so the body-class mutation is outside the hydrated component tree.

Hydrate the existing server markup with provideClientHydration(). Do not use ngSkipHydration as the default integration strategy; Angular documents it as a last-resort workaround that destroys and re-renders the skipped component.

For an initial application-wide boundary, wait for ApplicationRef.whenStable(), then one animation frame, before importing govuk-frontend and calling initAll with the application root as scope. This lets Angular finish post-hydration cleanup first.

If the application uses incremental hydration, initialise each boundary only after that boundary is hydrated. The fixture disables incremental hydration because it uses one application-wide enhancement scope.
Every journey must remain usable without the client bundle. Apply the service Content Security Policy nonce or hash to the early inline body-class script.
lifecycle: Initial render: server-render and hydrate first, wait for application stability and the following animation frame, then initialise the stable GOV.UK boundary once.
Later insertion: mount a fresh passive Angular leaf component containing complete unenhanced markup, then use afterNextRender in its write phase to initialise only that new host.

Do not change inputs, signals, bindings or projected content inside an enhanced boundary. OnPush limits checks but does not make changing templates safe after an external library has mutated their DOM.

To replace enhanced content, destroy the complete Angular component host and create a new host. Prefer full-page navigation for frequently changing interactive regions because GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 has no general public destroy lifecycle.
Test server HTML with JavaScript disabled, real hydration statistics, hydration mismatch diagnostics, mouse and keyboard behaviour, focus, whole-boundary replacement and a clean browser console.
adapters.pageTemplateIntro: Keep the `<html class="govuk-template">` page shell and early body support script in `src/index.html`, outside the Angular root. Use a static leaf component for complete GOV.UK markup. Bootstrap the identical tree with hydration providers shared by the server, then delay the initial GOV.UK Frontend import until Angular has stabilised and completed a browser frame.

adapters.name: Svelte
adapters.description: This adapter server-renders official GOV.UK markup with Svelte 5, hydrates that markup unchanged, and starts GOV.UK Frontend enhancement from a client-only onMount boundary. Enhanced descendants remain static because GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 mutates their DOM and exposes no general teardown API.
adapters.fixtureDescription: The development SSR and hydration fixture starts with `npm run fixture:serve:svelte` and renders `fixtures/svelte/App.svelte`. It exercises Button, Text input and Accordion with Svelte 5.57.0 and GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0. The fixture is test evidence, not package payload or a starter application.
requirements: Render complete GOV.UK page and component markup with Svelte SSR or prerendering. Do not make a client-only mount the only path to content, form controls or essential actions.

Translate official HTML into Svelte markup mechanically. Preserve elements, GOV.UK classes, IDs, for attributes, data-module attributes and ARIA relationships; Svelte uses the normal HTML class and for names.

Keep GOV.UK Frontend-enhanced descendants static after initialisation. Do not put reactive expressions, bindings, keyed or conditional blocks, transitions or Svelte event handlers inside markup that GOV.UK Frontend will mutate.
Use a small wrapper component as the enhancement boundary, capture its initial children, and keep stateful Svelte controls outside it. Replace the entire keyed boundary when new content is required.
Use the pinned govuk-frontend component CSS and JavaScript. Portable tokens remain for service-owned extensions and interoperability, not for recreating GOV.UK components.
Keep native form controls and server-rendered validation. Confirm separately that the service may use GDS Transport, the GOV.UK crown and other protected identity assets.
assetSetup: Install the reviewed implementation with npm install govuk-frontend@6.5.0 --save-exact and use a Svelte version supported by the host application. The fixture pins svelte@5.57.0 only to make its evidence reproducible.
Use the SvelteKit adapter and SSR or prerender configuration appropriate to the deployment, or compile separate Svelte client and server entry points in a custom host.
Import GOV.UK Frontend Sass or CSS through the host build, or copy dist/govuk/govuk-frontend.min.css to a public path. Copy dist/govuk/assets to the URL expected by the compiled CSS.
Import govuk-frontend only inside onMount or other browser-only code. The package references browser globals and must not be eagerly evaluated by the server runtime.
Load GOV.UK Frontend styles before service styles. Do not replace component CSS with tokens or a Svelte component library, and do not hotlink Design System assets.
rendering: Use the SvelteKit SSR or prerender pipeline for production. A custom renderer can call render from svelte/server with code compiled for the server, then place its head and body output into the page shell.

Hydrate server-rendered output with hydrate from svelte and the identical component tree and data. Set recover: false while developing and testing so a mismatch fails instead of discarding the server DOM.
Keep the early body support script outside the Svelte hydration target so its intentional class change cannot create a hydration mismatch.
Keep deterministic IDs and valid HTML between server and client. Svelte checks invalid element placement because browser HTML repair can break its structural assumptions.
Render Error summary, inline errors, safe submitted values, Accordion content and Tabs content on the server. GOV.UK Frontend applies disclosure state only after hydration.
progressiveEnhancement: Place the official body-class detection snippet immediately after the opening body element in the server page shell, before the Svelte hydration target.
Hydrate the existing server markup with hydrate, not mount. A client-only mount replaces the progressive-enhancement baseline instead of adopting it.
Initialise GOV.UK Frontend from onMount because Svelte does not run that hook during server rendering. Wait for tick and the next animation frame, then initialise only the stable boundary scope.

Keep the onMount callback synchronous so it can return a cleanup function. Run asynchronous initialisation in a nested function and use the cleanup to prevent late initialisation after the boundary unmounts.
Every journey must remain usable without the client bundle. Apply the service Content Security Policy nonce or hash to the early inline body-class script.
lifecycle: Initial render: server-render and hydrate first, then let the boundary's one-time onMount callback initialise GOV.UK Frontend after tick and the following animation frame.
Later insertion: render a fresh boundary containing complete unenhanced static markup and initialise only its wrapper. A keyed block can replace the whole boundary when its version changes.

Capture the initial children snippet and do not put reactive values inside enhanced descendants. Svelte's fine-grained updates are still unsafe when they target nodes or attributes already mutated by GOV.UK Frontend.
On removal, unmount the complete boundary. The synchronous onMount cleanup may cancel pending setup, but there is no general GOV.UK Frontend destroy lifecycle to call after initialisation.
Test server HTML with JavaScript disabled, hydration with recover disabled, retained DOM identity, mouse and keyboard behaviour, focus, whole-boundary replacement and a clean browser console.
adapters.pageTemplateIntro: Keep the `<html class="govuk-template">` shell and early body support script in the server template, outside the Svelte root. The following server and client entry points render and hydrate the same `App.svelte`; the app places complete static GOV.UK markup inside the boundary shown below.

// server.js import { render } from 'svelte/server' import App from './App.svelte' const { body, head } = await render(App) const document = ` ${head}
${body}
` // client.js — compile this as a separate browser entry import { hydrate } from 'svelte' import App from './App.svelte' const target = document.querySelector('#svelte-root') if (!target) throw new Error('Svelte root was not found') hydrate(App, { target, recover: false })
adapters.dynamicExampleIntro: Use a client-only boundary like this around complete static GOV.UK component markup. Capture the initial children so parent updates cannot substitute the snippet; when content must change, replace the complete boundary with a new keyed instance.

adapters.name: Astro
adapters.description: This adapter renders official GOV.UK markup as Astro's build-time or on-demand HTML, then adds only the GOV.UK Frontend client script needed for progressive enhancement. Native `.astro` components have no client runtime, so stable server output is the default rather than a hydration exception.
adapters.fixtureDescription: The development static-rendering fixture starts with `npm run fixture:serve:astro` and renders `fixtures/astro/src/pages/index.astro`. It exercises Button, Text input and Accordion with Astro 7.3.2 and GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0. The fixture is test evidence, not package payload or a starter application, and requires Node 22.12 or newer as required by Astro 7.
requirements: Render complete GOV.UK page and component markup with native `.astro` components at build time or on demand. Do not make a client island or server-island replacement the only path to content, form controls or essential actions.

Translate official HTML into Astro templates mechanically. Preserve elements, GOV.UK classes, IDs, for attributes, data-module attributes and ARIA relationships; native `.astro` templates use normal HTML class and for names.

Prefer native Astro components for GOV.UK markup because they render to HTML without a client runtime. Do not add a UI-framework island only to reproduce an official component that GOV.UK Frontend already enhances.

Never use client:only for essential GOV.UK content. If a React, Svelte or other framework island is genuinely required, use a server-rendering client directive and follow that framework adapter's externally managed DOM boundary rules.
Use the pinned govuk-frontend component CSS and JavaScript. Portable tokens remain for service-owned extensions and interoperability, not for recreating GOV.UK components.
Keep native form controls and server-rendered validation. Confirm separately that the service may use GDS Transport, the GOV.UK crown and other protected identity assets.
assetSetup: Install the reviewed implementation with npm install govuk-frontend@6.5.0 --save-exact and use an Astro version supported by the host application. The fixture pins astro@7.3.2 only to make its evidence reproducible.

Import the explicit compiled stylesheet from `govuk-frontend/dist/govuk/govuk-frontend.min.css` in Astro frontmatter, or copy that file and `dist/govuk/assets` to stable public URLs and load it with a link element.

Astro 7's Vite toolchain uses Lightning CSS minification by default, which rejects the legacy `@media (min-width: 0\0)` compatibility syntax in GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0's compiled CSS. When importing that CSS, set `vite.build.cssMinify` to `esbuild` and keep esbuild installed, or serve the official compiled file without rebundling it.

Put `import('govuk-frontend')` in an attribute-free processed Astro script so npm imports are bundled, emitted as modules and deduplicated. Never evaluate GOV.UK Frontend in component frontmatter because frontmatter runs on the server.
Load GOV.UK Frontend styles before service styles. Do not replace component CSS with tokens or another component library, and do not hotlink Design System assets.
rendering: Use Astro's default prerendering for static routes or an official deployment adapter for on-demand rendering. Both paths must return complete semantic HTML before client JavaScript runs.

Keep GOV.UK page and component markup in native `.astro` templates wherever possible. Component frontmatter is server-only and is stripped from the browser response; a client directive is neither needed nor valid on a native Astro component.
Keep deterministic IDs and valid HTML across shared layouts and components. Do not duplicate IDs when a reusable component appears more than once on a page.

Render Error summary, inline errors, safe submitted values, Accordion content and Tabs content into the initial response. GOV.UK Frontend applies disclosure state only after its processed client script runs.

Do not put essential enhanced controls behind server:defer unless the fallback remains usable and application code initialises the completed island exactly once after its replacement markup is connected.
progressiveEnhancement: Place the official body-class detection snippet in an `is:inline` script immediately after the opening body element so support classes exist before the processed enhancement bundle runs.
Place complete markup before an attribute-free processed script. Astro bundles npm imports, emits the script as a module and deduplicates it when its component is reused.
Import GOV.UK Frontend only in browser code and call initAll once with a stable Astro page or component boundary as scope. Surface initialisation errors to application monitoring and tests.

For ordinary multi-page navigation, initialise once on each new document. When ClientRouter is enabled, retain a single module listener and initialise each replacement boundary on astro:page-load, which fires after the new page and blocking assets have loaded.
Every journey must remain usable without the enhancement bundle. Apply the service Content Security Policy nonce or hash to the early inline support script.
lifecycle: Initial document: render complete native Astro HTML, run the early support snippet, then let the processed module script initialise the connected boundary once.
ClientRouter navigation: bundled module scripts execute only once, so listen for astro:page-load and use a WeakSet to initialise the new boundary without reinitialising retained DOM.

Do not apply transition:persist to a GOV.UK Frontend-enhanced boundary or its descendants. Astro can move persisted nodes into a new document, but GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 has no general public destroy or reconcile lifecycle for page-specific changes.

Later insertion: wrap complete unenhanced markup in a fresh boundary and initialise only that connected element. For a reusable insertion primitive, use a custom element whose connectedCallback performs guarded scoped initialisation.

Test built or on-demand HTML with JavaScript disabled, scoped initialisation, ClientRouter navigation when enabled, mouse and keyboard behaviour, focus, replacement boundaries and a clean browser console.
adapters.pageTemplateIntro: Use a native Astro layout or page so the `<html class="govuk-template">` shell and complete GOV.UK markup are emitted at build time or on demand. Import the official component CSS in frontmatter, keep the early support script inline, and put the processed enhancement script after the boundary.

adapters.dynamicExampleIntro: For independently inserted native Astro fragments, use a custom-element boundary like this. Astro deduplicates the processed definition script, while the browser runs connectedCallback for every new boundary instance.
adapters.dynamicExample:
<!-- GovukFrontendBoundary.astro -->
<govuk-frontend-boundary>
  <slot />
</govuk-frontend-boundary>

<script>
  const initialisedScopes = new WeakSet<Element>()

  class GovukFrontendBoundary extends HTMLElement {
    connectedCallback() {
      if (initialisedScopes.has(this)) return
      initialisedScopes.add(this)
      void this.initialise()
    }

    private async initialise() {
      try {
        const { initAll } = await import('govuk-frontend')
        if (!this.isConnected) {
          initialisedScopes.delete(this)
          return
        }
        initAll({
          scope: this,
          onError(error) { throw error }
        })
      } catch (error) {
        initialisedScopes.delete(this)
        queueMicrotask(() => { throw error })
      }
    }
  }

  if (!customElements.get('govuk-frontend-boundary')) {
    customElements.define('govuk-frontend-boundary', GovukFrontendBoundary)
  }
</script>
